**amux** — agent mux — the tmux-native, agent-first terminal for macOS · `status: alpha`

> amux is a native macOS terminal whose every workspace is a real tmux session on a dedicated `tmux -L amux` server, so sessions outlive the app. It projects tmux windows and panes into native Ghostty surfaces over control mode (`-CC`), and correlates Claude Code / Codex / Gemini hook events through the muxa daemon so the sidebar shows which agent is working, waiting, or errored. It is a friendly fork of [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux) and inherits its workspace UI, socket control plane, and SSH tmux mirror.

**Not for:** Linux or Windows · running as a plugin inside another terminal · replacing tmux itself · a hosted or web-based terminal

## Flows

| Flow | When |
| --- | --- |
| **onboard — New here (default)** | what is amux, install, build, first run, requirements |
| integrate — Drive it from something else | socket, CLI, hooks, automation, SSH, remote, sidebar extension, `cmux.json` |
| troubleshoot — When it misbehaves | crash, hang, lag, 100% CPU, beachball, blank, stale, does not resume, error |
| contribute — Work on the code | PR, test, lint, submodule, localization, pbxproj |

## onboard — top 5 FAQ

1. Is this a fork of Ghostty? → `upstream-faq` ↪ *So what is amux forked from?*
2. So what is amux forked from? → `readme`, `upstream-faq`
3. Does it work with the agent I already use? → `upstream-faq`, `agent-hooks`
4. If it is just tmux underneath, why not run tmux? → `readme`, `upstream-faq`
5. Will it touch my `~/.tmux.conf` or my existing tmux sessions? → `readme`

*(Source for all of the above: `AGENT_GUIDE.md`. Note: the overview, the Not-for line, and `status: alpha` carry maintainer TODO comments in the file — unconfirmed by the maintainer.)*

turns.send: what's the difference between amux and cmux? why is there a fork?
turns.text:
Routing: onboard FAQ *"So what is amux forked from?"* → `readme`, `upstream-faq`. Opening `README.md`.**What amux adds** (`README.md`):

| | cmux (upstream) | amux |
|---|---|---|
| Session backing | app-owned workspaces | workspace **==** a real tmux session on a dedicated `tmux -L amux` server — survives quitting the app |
| tmux control mode | used only for the **SSH** mirror | that same `-CC` mirror **generalized into a local engine** |
| Agents | agent notifications | **muxa/muxad** daemon correlates Claude Code / Codex / Gemini hook events to panes → live badges (*working · waiting · error*), **attend** = jump to longest-blocked agent (⌘⇧J) |
| CLI parity | — | `tmux -L amux attach` from any terminal; splits made either side appear in both |
| Branding/dist | cmux | own bundle, bundled tmux 3.7b + muxad, first-run wizard, signed dmg (`v0.1.0-alpha`) |

**What it inherits:** the Ghostty rendering stack, workspace UI, and socket control plane. "Upstream is merged periodically," and the original cmux README is preserved at `docs/upstream-cmux-README.md` (`README.md` § *Relationship to cmux*). License changes to **GPL-3.0-or-later** for the fork.

**Why the fork** — the README calls it a "friendly fork" and never states a motive in words; the stated architecture is the answer: amux inverts the ownership model so tmux owns session existence and muxad owns agent state, and amux.app is a *projection* of those two sources of truth. That's a foundational change, not a feature you bolt onto cmux. *(Inference from `README.md` § How it fits together — the "why" itself is unverified.)*

turns.send: typing feels laggy and one core is pegged at 100%
turns.text:
Routing: troubleshoot FAQ *"Typing feels laggy"* + *"pegs a CPU core"* → `agent-notes` (= `AGENTS.md`, symlink to `CLAUDE.md`, already in context) and `changelog`.**Two distinct rules cover this** (`AGENTS.md` → symlink of `CLAUDE.md`, § Pitfalls):

**Typing lag — the three latency-sensitive paths.** Anything added here runs per keystroke:
- `WindowTerminalHostView.hitTest()` in `Sources/TerminalWindowPortal.swift` — called on *every* event including keyboard. All divider/sidebar/drag routing must stay inside the `isPointerEvent` guard.
- `TabItemView` in `Sources/ContentView.swift` — relies on `Equatable` + `.equatable()` to skip body re-eval. Adding an `@EnvironmentObject`/`@ObservedObject`/`@Binding`, reading `tabManager`/`notificationStore` in the body, or dropping `.equatable()` at the ForEach call site kills it.
- `TerminalSurface.forceRefresh()` in `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift` — no allocations, file I/O, or string formatting.
- Also: never add an app-level display link or manual `ghostty_surface_draw` loop.

**Pegged core — the two spin-loop shapes.** (a) *Snapshot boundary*: below a `LazyVStack`/`List`/`ForEach`, no view may hold an `ObservableObject`/`@Observable` — not even a plain `let store:`. Rows get value snapshots + closure bundles (reference pattern: `IndexSectionActions` in `Sources/SessionIndexView.swift`). An orthogonal `@Published` change otherwise invalidates every row and thrashes `LazyLayoutViewCache` ([#2586](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/issues/2586)). (b) *No state mutation in view-body computations* — no `@Published` write, `Task { @MainActor in store.x = … }`, or `DispatchQueue.main.async` store write reachable from `body`. Prior instances in `CHANGELOG.md`: extension sidebar re-render loop (#6341), ContentView publisher feedback loop (#3028), FileExplorer update loop on macOS 26 (#5786).

*Unverified / off-manifest:* your branch has `Sources/TerminalController.swift`, `TerminalController+RemoteTmux.swift`, and `RemoteTmuxController.swift` modified — if the lag is new, that's where I'd look first. Want me to diff those against the base ref for per-keystroke work, or would sampling the pegged thread help more? (Sampling isn't in Tasks — I'd need your go-ahead.)

turns.send: I want to drive it from another program — is there a socket or an API?
turns.text:
Routing: integrate FAQ *"What can I actually drive over the socket?"* → `cli`, `events`.**Yes — a unix socket is the primary API**, with a CLI that's a thin client over it (`docs/cli-contract.md`).

**Three layers you can target:**
- **Raw v2 methods** — `cmux rpc <method> [json]` calls any socket method directly. `cmux capabilities` prints the server's method list as JSON; `cmux ping` checks connectivity; `cmux identify` prints server identity + caller context (`cli-contract.md:108–116`).
- **`amux` product verbs** — same socket/auth/JSON plumbing, agent-first: `ls`, `new [<task> --repo/--base/--branch/--worktree]`, `attach`, `attend`, `send`, `review`, `kill` (`cli-contract.md:36–54`). `amux send --workspace <ref> <text>` is the headless prompt — lands in the session's active pane, **no attach, no focus steal** (`README.md:31`).
- **Event stream** — `cmux events` emits newline-delimited JSON. Filter by `names`/`categories`; every frame carries `seq`, `boot_id`, `id`, `name`, `category`, `source`, `occurred_at`, plus `workspace_id`/`surface_id`/`pane_id`/`window_id` and a `payload`. Resume with `after_seq` + `boot_id`, dedupe on `id`; heartbeats on by default (`docs/events.md:34–161`). Catalog includes `workspace.created/selected/closed/renamed/moved`, `workspace.prompt.submitted`, `surface.created/selected/focused`, `window.keyed/unkeyed`.

**Wiring:** `--socket <path>` or `CMUX_SOCKET_PATH` (`CMUX_SOCKET` is a deprecated alias — setting both to different values is a hard error); `--password` or `CMUX_SOCKET_PASSWORD`; `--json` and `--id-format refs|uuids|both`. Handles accept UUIDs, refs like `workspace:2`, or indexes anywhere a window/workspace/pane/surface/tab is taken (`cli-contract.md:17–21, 56–72`). Inside an amux terminal, `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID`/`CMUX_SURFACE_ID` supply default context.

*Heads-up: `docs/cli-contract.md` is modified in your working tree, so this reflects your branch, not `main`.*
